description: Returns ONE post/page’s body EXACTLY as stored — the source an edit has to be written against, block comments, shortcodes, HTML entities and all. ⛔ Not a rendering: preview-markdown returns the .md twin, which is what an AI client reads, and check-page returns a grade; neither can be edited and sent back. This is the FIRST half of changing anything on a page — read it here, then send edit-content an exact passage from what you got. `format` says whether the body is block markup or classic HTML, because a paragraph is wrapped in comments in one and bare in the other. `editable` is false when this body is not the thing to change: a page builder owns the layout, or somebody has the post open in the editor right now — `note` says which, in words you can repeat to the owner.
name: agentimus-read-content

builder.description: The page builder that owns this page’s layout, empty when none does. Not empty ⇒ the body below is not what visitors see.

content.description: The body, byte for byte as stored. Copy anchors for edit-content from HERE.

editable.description: TRUE when edit-content can act on this body — no builder, nobody editing.

format.description: "blocks" when the body is block markup, "classic" when it is plain HTML.

alt.description: Its description as stored, empty when it has none.

attachmentId.description: Its media library id, 0 when the picture belongs to no attachment — pasted in, or hotlinked. Its alt still needs writing.

captioned.description: TRUE when the author wrote a caption under it. ⭐ A captioned picture marked decorative is a contradiction the author wrote themselves — that pair is what `needs: "blank-alt"` reports, and it is the one empty alt this tool will write over without replace.

decorative.description: TRUE when the tag carries alt="" — the standard way of saying the picture holds no meaning a reader needs. ⛔ On its own that is a decision, not a gap: the checks do not flag it and neither should you. Read it with `captioned`.

index.description: Its position among the images on this page, from 1. This is what describe-content-image takes, and the only aim that is never ambiguous.

needs.description: "no-alt" when the tag has no alt attribute at all, "file-name" when its description is only the file name, "blank-alt" when it is marked decorative (alt="") yet carries a caption — which is the author saying it means something — and empty when nothing is wanted. These are the images behind an alt_text row.

src.description: The address the tag points at.

lockedBy.description: Who has the post open in the editor right now, empty when nobody does. An edit made while somebody is editing gets overwritten by their autosave.

modified.description: When it was last saved (GMT). If this moves between your read and your edit, somebody else has been writing.

note.description: Anything that makes this body not the thing to edit, in plain words. Empty when there is nothing to say.

scheduledFor.description: When it goes live, in the site’s own timezone with its offset. Empty unless status is future.

title: Read a page’s body
